eligibility_note: Quantitative worker-level regressions and RIF/Oaxaca-Ransom decompositions on PIAAC for 22 countries (19 for wages). Exposure is worker-level ICT use at work (ICT in general); outcomes are task content (labour market) and wages/wage inequality (distribution). Meets the 10-economy rule. Caveat: the exposure is a worker-level questionnaire index, not a national adoption measure, and the data are a single cross-section.

income_group_note: No income-group analysis exists, so the entries are not income-group results (record says so). Number to fix: Russian Federation country effect in Table 7 is 0.297*** (col 1), 0.0140 (col 2, ICT added), 0.0125 (col 3, ICT x country). risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree: single cross-section, no instrument or timing, ICT use and task content from the same respondent, yet the abstract says computer adoption 'leads to' the differences and ICT is a 'key significant driver'.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree: worker-level PCA index from a self-chosen item subset, not a national adoption measure, and partly mechanically related to abstract task content; moderate is defensible (could be argued serious for the country-level claim).
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree: all PIAAC 2011-12 countries with usable data, rich-country heavy, three countries dropped for wages, arbitrary three wage groups.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree: self-reported task frequencies, manual tasks cannot be split into routine/non-routine, and the effect falls to about 10% when manual tasks are included.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree: several RTI definitions and item subsets; both RTI versions are shown. The statement that the headline uses 'the definition with the stronger ICT result' is the record's characterisation (the paper explains the exclusion of manual tasks by measurement problems).
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree: both RTI definitions are reported, but the abstract features the 41%/25% figures from the manual-excluded index and the wage-inequality conclusion rests on graphs without tests.
risk_of_bias.why: Cross-sectional associations with causal wording and no strategy for reverse causation or unobservables; serious fits the guide.

problems: None invented. Only issues: Russia coefficient column (above), the 'five Eastern European countries and Russia' wording, and unverifiable 'all three comparisons' detail read from a figure. Paper is a draft version (Nov 2015, FEDEA working paper).

eligibility_note: Structural CES model estimated by GMM/IV with its own data (EU KLEMS, 11 OECD economies, 1980-2005, four non-primary sectors); exposure is ICT capital (ICCT) and its falling price; outcomes are gender/skill wage gaps and labour income shares (labour market, distribution). Meets 10-economy rule. All economies high income, no income-group comparison. Headline effects are model-based counterfactuals.

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree: first differences remove country effects and IV (lagged group population, lagged ICCT price) address simultaneity, but exclusion is untested and effects are counterfactuals from a maintained nested-CES structure; note the second instrument is the ICT price itself, so identification of the substitution parameters relies on ICT price variation being exogenous.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree: EU KLEMS ICT capital and investment price are direct measures; rental prices are constructed.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree: 11 high-income countries, 1980-2005, all countries with data, outside the smartphone/broadband/AI period.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree: wages from compensation per hour adjusted for age/education composition; skill defined by college completion.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree: results depend on nesting order, consumption elasticity 0.9 and instrument choice (lagged population chosen because 'more precise'); robustness shown.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree: robustness, country results and null results reported; headline in introduction uses unit-elastic scenario and the abstract says 'declining labor shares' although the aggregate effect is small in the exogenous case.
risk_of_bias.why: Structural IV design with extensive robustness and bootstrap SEs; counterfactuals rely on model structure, so moderate is appropriate.

problems: No invented numbers found. Flag: record title is another version's title; direction for aggregate labour share should not be a flat 'null'. Pagination refers to arXiv v9.

eligibility_note: Quantitative with own FE and convergence estimation, AI exposure (government AI readiness), 28 economies with explicit AE vs EMDE comparison, so the economy-count and design criteria hold. The outcome criterion fails: the dependent variables are Trade/GDP, merchandise trade/GDP and digital-service trade/GDP, which are not output/productivity, labour-market, poverty/distribution, living-standard or resource-cost outcomes. Digital versus merchandise trade composition is not structural change of the economy (no sectoral output or employment shares), and the GE measures are cross-country dispersion of trade ratios, not income distribution. Recommend exclusion (at most borderline).

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree: FE regression of trade ratios on a readiness index with causal wording ('AI can accelerate trade'), no instrument, four years, plausible reverse causation.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree: AIRI measures government readiness to deliver AI public services; only 2023 scores shown, so within-country variation 2020-2023 is not documented.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree: 28 hand-picked 'representative' countries, 4 COVID-era years, extrapolated trade values (Japan, USA, Viet Nam 2023; Lao PDR whole period).
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree: trade ratios are standard but are not productivity or welfare outcomes, GDP also a control, extrapolated values included.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree: controls differ across columns, stars inconsistent with SEs (ln REER -0.0832, SE 0.0712 marked *), convergence regressions with SE 0.0043 and within R2 about 0.99 on 36-84 observations; serious is right.
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree: control results 'not discussed', robustness not shown, near-zero between R2 not discussed, column order inconsistent with text.
risk_of_bias.why: Thin identification, mismeasured exposure and small hand-picked sample; serious (the convergence regressions border on critical).

problems: Record is faithful to the tables. Main problem is eligibility (outcome not in the listed families). Also note inconsistency between Table A2 column order and text order, and the unsupported claim in the abstract that inequality in digital trade is rising in EMDEs (true only after 2020).

eligibility_note: Quantitative panel (TWFE, system GMM, lags) on 63 low/middle-income economies 2005-2019; exposure is an AI Capability Index (AI-related hardware imports plus ICT/electricity/finance indicators), outcome is labour productivity; income-group comparison (low vs lower-middle) included. Eligible under AI (3+ economies) and under ICT in general, since five of six index components are general ICT or infrastructure indicators.

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree: TWFE, GMM with internal instruments and 1-6 year lags are used and the authors disclaim causality, but reverse causation and time-varying omitted factors are not excluded (paper says GMM 'does not fully address' these); moderate.
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree: first principal component of six variables of which one is AI-related imports; loadings are similar (about 0.33-0.48), so the index is largely general digital/infrastructure development, imports include laptops, phones and monitors, and the authors state it does not capture realised AI use.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree: 63 of 80 LMICs retained for data completeness, readiness variables come from a MICE-imputed dataset, country list not given in the main text, pre-generative-AI period.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: agree: labour productivity is defined inconsistently (GDP/total labour force in Table 1; GDP per capita divided by total employment in Sec 4.3; real GDP per worker in Sec 5.1).
risk_of_bias.specification: agree: flow vs stock, broad vs narrow lists, many control sets and estimators; headline TWFE stable across controls. The record's 'about 80 specs' is not stated in the text (unverifiable count).
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree: non-significant interactions and controls are reported; a single outcome; no pre-registration.
risk_of_bias.why: The exposure measure largely does not capture AI, which makes 'serious' appropriate under the guide even though the design is otherwise a standard panel with GMM robustness.

problems: One correction (GMM flow range). Record's '(about 80 specs)' count is not found in the text. Narrow-index description 'AI-hardware-only' may overstate how narrow it is. Otherwise faithful to the text.
